runs.t: •  Say: I work at a restaurant.

slides.notes:
Welcome. Say: "Today: jobs." Point to the picture: "He is a cook."
Say at the start: "Everyone has an answer. You can say: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now." Write these 3 answers on the board and leave them there.
Never ask about pay, bosses, or work papers. Never ask where someone works if they don't offer it.

slides.title: What's Your Job?

runs.t: I can say: I work at a factory.
I can ask: What do you do?
I can answer: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
I can say: I don't work now.
a or an?  The sh sound: cashier

slides.notes:
Click to show each goal, one at a time. Read it aloud. Learners repeat.
Goal 1: point to the job pictures: "I'm a cook. I'm an office worker."
Goal 4: nod for "Yes, I do." Shake your head for "No, I don't."
Goal 5: "I'm a student" and "I'm a homemaker" are good answers too.
Letters & Numbers at 7:15: a or an, the sh sound (cashier), and job signs.

slides.title: Today's Goals

runs.t: Do you have brothers or sisters?

slides.notes:
Pairs. Review of last week (family). 15 learners: 7 pairs + 1 group of 3. 7–8 learners: 3–4 pairs. Late arrivals join any pair.
Model with one learner: "Do you have brothers or sisters?" Learner: "Yes, I do. I have two brothers."
Point to the picture: "Who's this?" Click: "This is my mother." Click again for the next line. Learners can use their family or Ana's family.
Partners switch, then find a new partner. Help: "Can you repeat, please?" "How do you spell it?"
Last 3 minutes: homework check. Partners show each other the Lesson 4 homework. Look at item 2 (do / don't).
If behind: one partner only.

slides.notes:
Say first: "Today: jobs. What do you do? You can say: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now."
Click to show each picture. Point and say the word. Learners repeat 2 times.
Act out each job. Learners copy the action. Cook: stir a pot. Cashier: scan and count money. Driver: turn a wheel. Cleaner: sweep.
cleaner = housekeeper. Both words are OK.

slides.title: Before You Listen

runs.t: Listen. Write the letter of the job.

slides.notes:
Listen 1. Learners match each person to a job picture. They write the letter: 1 Rosa ___, 2 Marco ___, 3 Marco's wife ___, 4 Rosa's husband ___.
Pairs compare: "Show your partner." Then click to show each number on its picture: 1 Rosa = b (cashier), 2 Marco = a (cook), 3 Marco's wife = d (nurse), 4 Rosa's husband = c (mechanic).
Answer key: 1 b, 2 a, 3 d, 4 c.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 3: Listening; Answer key, Listening Task A).

slides.title: Listening A

runs.t: Listen again. Circle Yes or No.

slides.notes:
Listen 2 (Task B). Learners circle Yes or No.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer: 1 Yes, 2 Yes, 3 No (he doesn't work in the morning), 4 No (at a store), 5 Yes.
Ask: "Where does Rosa work?" Point to the cashier picture: "At a store."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Answer key, Listening Task B).
slides.title: Listening B

slides.notes:
Listen 3 (Task C). Learners write do, don't, or does.
Pairs compare. Then click to show each answer: 1 do, 2 don't, 3 do, 4 does.
The preview line: play the end again or read it: "Does your wife work, too? Yes, she does. She's a nurse."
Say: "Does = a question about he or she. Level 2 practices it. Today: only listen."
If behind: play the audio 2 times, and do Task C together.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 3: Listening; Answer key, Listening Task C).
slides.title: Listening C

slides.notes:
Show the Grammar page. The left side is the question. The right side is the answer. Point left, then right.
Ask: "What do you do?" Click: "I'm a cook." Write on the board: a cook, a driver / an office worker.
Say: before a, e, i, o, u → an. Hold up one finger: "a cook."
Click for each answer. Point to the 3 "everyone" answers: I'm a student. I'm a homemaker. I don't work now. These are good answers.
The big mistake: "I'm cook." In English a job needs a or an: I'm a cook.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 1; Teacher notes).

slides.title: What do you do?

slides.notes:
Ask: "Where do you work?" Click: "I work at a restaurant. I work at a factory." Point to the place pictures.
Click again: at a store, at home. "I work at home" is a good answer.
Right side: an office (o is a vowel, so an). "In an office" is also fine; don't correct it.
Questions need do: Where do you work? (not "Where you work?").
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Box 2; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Where do you work?

slides.notes:
Box 3: ask "Do you work at night?" Nod: "Yes, I do." Shake your head: "No, I don't." The same as "Do you have kids?" in Lesson 4.
Click to show each answer.
Box 4 (top right): "I work at night. I don't work in the morning." Use the board: ✓ work / ✗ don't work.
Check question: "Do you work on weekends?" (Yes, I do. / No, I don't.)
Common mistake: "I no work." Say: "I don't work."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 4: Grammar Q&A, Boxes 3 and 4).
slides.title: Do you work at night?

runs.t: You don't need to write it.

slides.notes:
Preview box (1–2 min, no practice needed). Read the question. Click: "Yes, she does. She's a nurse." The class repeats once.
Click again for the other answers. Read them once. The class repeats.
Say: "Level 2. Only listen today." Don't test it and don't explain the -s in works.
If a learner says "She work at a hospital," just repeat it correctly: "Yes, she works at a hospital."
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 4: Preview box; Grammar: Preview; Teacher notes).

runs.t: Write a, an, at, do, or don't.

slides.notes:
Learners write one word on each line. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer: 1 a, 2 an, 3 at, 4 do, 5 don't.
Pair drill (last 3–4 min): A asks from the left side of the Grammar page; B answers from the right side about a picture card (or about themselves). Then switch.
If behind: skip the pair drill. It becomes homework, and Talk Time practices the same questions.

slides.title: a, an, at, do, don't?

runs.t: Do you work at night? Yes, I work.
I work in a restaurant at night

slides.notes:
Read each "Don't say" line. Shake your head. Click to show the correct line. Learners repeat it.
The big mistake this week: "I'm cook." A job needs a or an: I'm a cook. Correct by holding up one finger: "a cook."
Questions need do: Where do you work? "No" is don't: I don't work on Sunday.
Workplaces use at: at a restaurant, at a factory, at home. Streets use on: on Main Street.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Grammar: Common mistakes; Teacher notes).

slides.title: Common Mistakes

runs.t: No, I'm not. / Yes, I am!

slides.notes:
Part 1, guessing game (4 min). Groups of 3–4. Each group has a set of job picture cards.
Model it first: you act out "driver"; the class guesses. "Are you a cook?" "No, I'm not." "Are you a driver?" "Yes, I am!"
Click to show each step. One learner takes a card (don't show it) and acts out the job. The others ask: "Are you a ___?" The winner takes the next card.
Learners who can't read or write yet can play this game fully.
If behind: do only the guessing game.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 1; Student Pages: Talk Time 1).

slides.title: Talk Time

runs.t: A: Do you work at night?
3. Do you work at a restaurant?
4. Do you work in the morning?

slides.notes:
Part 2, Find Someone Who (6 min). Everyone stands with the Talk Time page.
Model it: "Do you work at night?" → "No, I don't." → ask someone else → "Yes, I do." → write that name. Click to show the B line.
Learners write a name when someone says "Yes, I do." For line 6 (Do you work now?), write a name for "No, I don't." One name per line; a different person for each line if possible.
Finish: 2–3 learners report one line: "Ana works at night." (A preview of works; accept "Ana work at night" too.)
Learners who can't write yet ask the questions while a partner writes names, or they draw a check.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 5: Talk Time, Part 2; Student Pages: Talk Time 2).
slides.title: Find Someone Who

slides.notes:
Exit ticket (never skip): each learner says one sentence about work: "I'm a cook." / "I work at a factory." / "I'm a student." / "I don't work now."
Or learners write a or an for two words on the board: ___ cook, ___ office worker (a cook, an office worker).
Homework (10 minutes): open the Homework page. Do item 1 together (the first sentence). Point to each instruction.
Homework: 1) I'm a / an ___. I work at ___. (or I'm a student / I'm a homemaker / I don't work now); 2) a or an; 3) do or don't; 4) ask a family member or a friend: What do you do? Where do you work?; 5) review: one sentence about your family (or Ana's family).
Homework answers: item 2: 1 a, 2 an, 3 a, 4 an, 5 a. Item 3: do or don't, if it matches the learner's Yes / No.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Step 6: Exit Ticket + Homework; Student Pages: Homework; Answer key).

slides.title: Before You Go

slides.notes:
Letters & Numbers (10 min). Whole class, then pairs. Use the Letters & Numbers page.
Task A (2 min): point to the vowel letters a e i o u. Read the a column. Click to show each an word. Learners repeat.
An goes before a vowel sound: an office, an apartment. More from the page: a server, an ID card.
Task C (2 min): say sh like "Quiet!" (finger on lips). Then: she, shoe, cashier, English, wash. Learners repeat each word 2 times.
Spanish speakers often say ch (as in chair): show the difference with a long, soft "shhh."
Partners: A says a job, B says a or an + the job. Switch.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Letters & Numbers, Tasks A and C).
slides.title: a or an?

slides.notes:
Task B (2 min). Learners write a or an before each word. Then pairs check.
Click to show each answer circle: 1 a mechanic, 2 an office worker, 3 a factory, 4 an apartment, 5 a painter, 6 an email.
Say each answer. Learners repeat: "a mechanic."
Learners who can't read or write yet say the words with everyone and point.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Letters & Numbers, Task B; Answer key, Task B).

runs.t: NOW HIRING: the store wants new workers.
NOW HIRING: the store wants doctors.
EMPLOYEES ONLY: customers can go in.
EMPLOYEES ONLY: workers can go in.
Where do you see this sign?

slides.notes:
Task D (3 min). Point to each sign and read it: NOW HIRING. EMPLOYEES ONLY. Learners repeat.
Read each line. Learners circle Yes or No. Then click to show each answer: 1 Yes, 2 No, 3 No, 4 Yes.
Ask: "Where do you see this sign?" (a store window; a door at work).
Learners who can't read yet: read the signs aloud for them and let them answer by pointing.
If behind: do Tasks A and B only (skip this slide).

slides.title: Read the Signs

runs.t: a. I work at a factory.

slides.notes:
Progress Check (5 min). Individuals. Open the Progress Check page.
Part A: read the 5 words slowly, 2 times each: 1 cashier, 2 mechanic, 3 nurse, 4 factory, 5 server. Learners circle.
Parts B and C: learners match and write on their own. Help with the instructions only. Click to show the Part B answers when you check together: 1 c, 2 a, 3 d, 4 b.
Part C answers: 1 a, 2 an, 3 don't.
Part D: read each "I can…" line and point to the 3 faces: 😀 "I can do it." 🙂 "A little." 😐 "Not yet." Learners check one.
Score: A /5 + B /4 + C /3 = /12. This is not a test grade. Collect the pages. If behind: do it in Week 6 at 6:00.
Source: level1_curriculum/lesson5/Level1_Lesson5.md (Progress Check; Answer key).
